extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (attorneys, agents), applicants, and analysts looking at USPTO grant statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Explore and interpret USPTO grant-rate metrics (by tech center, art unit, group, and examiner) including the three-year grant rate, timelines, and examiner-level distributions to inform patent prosecution strategy or analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of statistics available
rubrics_metrics.description: We have statistics for tech centers, groups, art units, and examiners. Use the links below to see statistics about each one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site provides multiple aggregation levels (tech center, group, art unit, examiner) so users should choose the level appropriate to their analysis or prosecution strategy. No scoring guidance beyond the availability of these categories is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-year grant rate (3YGR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The three-year grant rate is the percentage of applications granted at three years after the first office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The timeline and table display 3YGR as the primary metric for comparing units/examiners. Interpretation: 3YGR measures grants observed within three years from the first office action; use it to compare relative grant likelihood over that window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tech Center grant rates (3YGR) — table entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Tech Center / Description / 3YGR: 1600 Biotechnology and Organic Chemistry — 61%; 1700 Chemical and Materials Engineering — 68%; 2100 Computer Architecture and Software — 80%; 2400 Networking, Multiplexing, Cable, and Cybersecurity — 84%; 2600 Communications — 86%; 2800 Semiconductors/Memory, Circuits/Measuring and Testing, Optics/Photocopying, Printing/Measuring and Testing — 87%; 2900 Design — 97%; 3600 Transportation, Construction, Electronic Commerce, Agriculture, National Security and License and Review — 74%; 3700 Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing, Gaming, and Medical Devices/Processes — 72%; 3900 Reexam/Abandonments — 56%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This table presents 3YGR by tech center (original wording preserved). Use these percentages to compare grant likelihood across tech centers. Be aware tech centers aggregate many art units and examiners; interpretation should account for domain differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant Rate Timeline (relative to first office action)
rubrics_metrics.description: Below is the grant rate timeline for USPTO, where the timeline is relative to the date of the first office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The timeline shows how grant rates evolve over time from the date of the first office action; the three-year point is used as a standard comparison. Use the timeline to assess timing dynamics in prosecution and when grants typically occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Histogram of examiner grant rates (weighted by number of cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Below is a weighted histogram (by number of cases) of the 3-year grant rates of the examiners in USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The histogram is weighted by case counts so high-volume examiners affect the distribution more. Summary statistics provided: average = 77% and standard deviation = 17%. Use these to understand variability across examiners and to benchmark individual examiners against the USPTO distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary statistics: average and standard deviation of examiner 3YGR
rubrics_metrics.description: The average is 77% and the standard deviation is 17%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These summary stats give a quick view of central tendency and dispersion of examiner-level 3YGRs. Use them to determine how typical or atypical a given examiner's grant rate is.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data accuracy / liability disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclaimer: We do not provide any guarantees as to the accuracy of the statistics presented above and under no circumstances will we be liable for any outcome resulting from your reliance on the above statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the statistics as informational rather than definitive. Verify critical decisions with primary USPTO sources or additional analysis; the provider disclaims responsibility for outcomes based on the data.
